title: CLV measurement protocol
not_an_experiment: CLV has no hypothesis, challenger or verdict. It defines how an already-published number is scored against the market, so it does not belong in the DUR register and carries no model_version.

capture_gate.rationale: Raw quotes begin and continue capturing immediately. Collecting early loses nothing; deciding early is the disciplined part.

covers: any CLV figure on a user-facing page
any CLV figure in a post, email or digest
any CLV summary statistic computed from captured quotes
publication_gate.not_covered: Row-level settlement into model_edges.clv_pp continues — it is bookkeeping under the already-shipped convention, not a published result.

disclosure: No historical CLV comparison was run while drafting. No alternative definition was evaluated against captured data. Every recommendation rests on argument from principle or precedent, never on which option produced a better number.

decided_rules.title: Raw capture is immediate, immutable and append-only
decided_rules.basis: matches prop_model_locks and pre_fight_snapshots trigger enforcement

decided_rules.title: A quote without a timestamp is not eligible
decided_rules.basis: cannot be placed relative to forecast or close

decided_rules.title: Non-market price guard, implied probability in [0.03, 0.97]
decided_rules.basis: added 2026-08-19 after a sentinel row flipped the sign of mean CLV across the first settleable batch

decided_rules.title: No substitution, no imputation for a missing close
One-sided or missing markets leave the observation unscored, and unscored counts are reported
decided_rules.basis: a coverage problem must not hide inside a favourable average

decided_rules.title: Duplicate and reposted markets deduplicate on (book, fight_id, fighter_id, quoted_at)
decided_rules.basis: all postings retained raw, distinguished by capture time

decided_rules.title: forecast_locked_at < close_quoted_at, strictly, in UTC
decided_rules.basis: no-lookahead; pre_fight_snapshots makes the publish-time forecast recoverable

decided_rules.title: Outcome independence — void and no-contest retained and scored; cancelled-before-close excluded, not scored zero
decided_rules.basis: CLV measures price, not result; scoring zero would pull summaries toward the middle

decided_rules.title: No CLV summary statistic before freeze
decided_rules.basis: a definition chosen after looking at data is not a preregistered definition

decided_rules.title: Publication gate — nothing on a surface until frozen
Provenance — a published figure names its protocol version and the script that produced it
decided_rules.basis: inherits the research register's standing rule

decided_rules.title: Copy governance — CLV wording follows COPY_STYLE.md
decided_rules.basis: Q-11 fixes substance, COPY_STYLE.md fixes wording

open_questions.question: what "closing line" means (+ staleness limit)
options: last quote before the book takes the market down
consensus at a fixed offset from scheduled start
open_questions.recommendation: last quote before scheduled start, subject to a staleness limit set from capture cadence

open_questions.question: eligible books and exclusion rules
options: fixed named list frozen at protocol freeze
open_questions.recommendation: fixed named list; DUR-001 already forbids selecting books after results are visible, and a fixed list makes that unbreakable rather than merely prohibited

open_questions.question: treatment of exchanges and prediction markets
open_questions.escalates_to: L3 if admitted to the primary consensus
open_questions.recommendation: exclude from the primary; commission-based pricing mixed into a vig-based consensus is cleanly neither

open_questions.question: how multiple books become one market probability
open_questions.recommendation: median — robust to one mispriced book, and the shipped implementation already takes the median book's own booked price rather than a reconstructed one
open_questions.note: best available price is the option that would most flatter CLV; that asymmetry is why it must be settled by argument now

open_questions.question: vigged or de-vigged
open_questions.why_l3: changes both the magnitude and the meaning of the published number, and conflicts with the shipped implementation
options: power de-vig both ends per DUR-001 Amendment 1
raw as primary, de-vigged as a frozen sensitivity
open_questions.recommendation: raw as primary, de-vigged as a frozen sensitivity once two-sided publish capture exists
open_questions.blocks: two-sided capture at publish time must start immediately — the de-vigged variant can never be backfilled

open_questions.question: does CFL evaluate its published probability or a hypothetical wager price
open_questions.why_l3: decides what the headline number is
options: bettor's CLV on the posted price
market anticipation of the published probability
open_questions.recommendation: both, with the term CLV reserved strictly for the price measure; market anticipation is a different quantity and must never carry the CLV label

open_questions.question: aggregation and weighting across fights and cards
open_questions.why_l3: equal-weight and stake-weight are different public claims, not different estimators of one thing
open_questions.recommendation: equal weight per fight; a stake weighting invents a staking strategy CFL does not publish in order to score it

open_questions.question: minimum sample before a summary is displayed
open_questions.why_l3: track-record.html already publishes a commitment to 100+ locked picks, so the protocol either adopts it or the copy changes
options: per-breakout floors as well as overall
open_questions.recommendation: 100 scored observations overall and the same floor on any breakout, following Factor Lab's MIN_SAMPLE pattern including its explicit 'not enough data yet' state

open_questions.question: confidence intervals and uncertainty
options: Wilson interval on the beat rate
open_questions.recommendation: report a cluster-robust interval on mean clv_pp and a Wilson interval on the beat rate; they answer different questions and the pair is harder to cherry-pick

open_questions.question: cancellation, rescheduling and late opponent change
open_questions.recommendation: score neither for a rescheduled fight, and exclude a fight whose opponent changed after the forecast lock; keyed mechanically on whether either fighter id changed

open_questions.question: how positive CLV may and may not be described publicly
options: adopt the may / may-never list in §3 Q-11 as written
stricter — descriptive reporting only, with no comparative framing of any kind
more permissive — allow comparison against public benchmarks once past the Q-08 floor
open_questions.recommendation: adopt the list as written; it permits the measurement to be stated plainly with its interval and n, and forbids every phrasing that converts a price measurement into a claim about winning money
never_permitted: any projection of profit, ROI or bankroll growth from a CLV figure
'beats the market', 'proven edge', or any phrasing converting a price measurement into a claim about winning money
a positive figure without its interval and its n
a favourable subset presented without the overall number beside it
any claim at all while the interval crosses zero — reported as 'we can't tell yet'

capture_requirements_that_cannot_be_back: book, fighter, American price and UTC capture instant on every quote
both sides captured at the publish instant
provider and feed version stored per quote
freeze_procedure: status becomes frozen, with the UTC instant and Reed as approver
the sha256 of the protocol markdown is recorded here and in the frozen-file tripwire
every open question is resolved in place, with rejected options retained as rejected
settle_clv.py is reconciled with the frozen rules
post_freeze_change_routes: a dated amendment recorded with both hashes and a reason, motivated_by_observed_results false and true
